title: Escrowed Feature Commitment Ledger and Timebox Playbook
creator: Asha Ramanathan
description:
Problem: Strategic (top-tier) accounts frequently request scoped features with implied deadlines. Engineering and PM teams struggle to (a) clearly record what was promised, (b) prioritize across multiple VIP asks, and (c) handle missed commitments without damaging relationships or burning engineering cycles.

Proposal: Create an 'Escrowed Feature Commitment Ledger' (EFCL) that sits inside the intake flow for high-touch accounts. When a feature is accepted into a VIP lane, an EFCL entry is created that: (1) records a precise scope (scope line items with mock examples), (2) timeboxes the commitment into a 2-8 week window with clearly stated acceptance criteria, (3) ties the commitment to an escrow token (a customer credit/priority point that can be redeemed or refunded on SLA miss), and (4) wires automatic rollback and fallback policies (degraded shipping, alternative timeline, PR-to-customer communication).

Objectives:
- Reduce ambiguity in VIP commitments; enable objective go/no-go decisions for scope changes.
- Give Sales/CS a predictable, auditable ledger entry they can present to customers (reduces informal 'we'll try' promises).
- Protect engineering capacity via explicit timeboxes and automatic de-escalation triggers.
- Provide measurable signals for OKRs: commit-on-time rate, average slip days, escrow redemption rate, customer satisfaction delta post-delivery.

Scope of work:
1) Intake form schema changes (Console + CS template) to capture structured scope + acceptance criteria + escrow amount.
2) Backend: EFCL lightweight datastore + API endpoints for CRUD and state transitions (proposed -> active -> shipped -> slipped -> refunded).
3) Console UI: EFCL dashboard in Top Accounts view with timeline, commitment health, and audit trail.
4) Playbook document: roles (PM, Eng lead, AE/CS), decision gates, fallback templates (customer-facing comms).
5) Telemetry: metrics pipeline to populate the OKR dashboard.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake creates a valid EFCL entry with scope and acceptance criteria at time of triage (manually or via AE).
- Engineering can opt a commitment into a 2-week, 4-week, or 8-week timebox with a default template.
- On missed commitment, escrow token moves to 'eligible for refund' and an automated communication draft is created for CS review.
- Dashboard surfaces all active commitments, their health (green/yellow/red), and a changelog with at least 3 prior state transitions.
- Telemetry emits events to the OKR pipeline and we have two KPIs in the OKR board: commit_on_time_rate and average_slip_days.
acceptance_criteria: Intake can attach an EFCL entry with structured scope and acceptance criteria
Timebox templates (2/4/8 weeks) selectable at triage and visible in EFCL entry
Escrow token state machine implemented with automated state transitions for slip/refund
Console shows active commitments with status badges and changelog entries
Events emitted to OKR telemetry: commit_on_time_rate and average_slip_days
implementation_notes: Backend ledger implemented as a lightweight service in the control plane; should be replication-safe for Private deployments
Use existing intake webhook from CS to prefill scope fields; add new structured schema version v2
Escrow token will map to an internal 'priority credit' integer; payments/refunds handled by Finance via separate flow
Fallback flows: automatic downgrade to 'scope-minimum' when slip > 5 business days unless exec override
SLA triggers: slip > 3 days -> auto-notify AE/CS; slip > 7 days -> create escalation bridge
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales/CS may overuse escrowed commitments leading to engineering churn; Mitigation: enforce quarterly quota on escrowed tokens and require AE manager approval
Risk: Complexity spikes for private deployments with stricter change controls; Mitigation: EFCL control-plane calls must be toggleable and respect on-prem privacy knobs
Risk: Legal concern around 'refund' semantics for escrow; Mitigation: consult Legal and Finance and keep escrow actions as 'priority credit' until policy ratified
Risk: Overhead for small requests; Mitigation: only accounts tagged as Top-3 or with active Enterprise contract can use EFCL
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): Q2 pilot with 5 strategic accounts (AE-signed); manual review gate by PM and Eng lead
Phase 1 (opt-in): Expand to Top-20 accounts with automated intake, beta dashboard; collect feedback for 6 weeks
Phase 2 (GA): Enable for all enterprise accounts and add telemetry to OKR boards; train CS and Sales via playbook
Contingency: If commit_on_time_rate < 60% at pilot end, freeze expansion and pivot to stricter approval flows
